claims.claim: A new Muslim makes ghusl in the first day or two (stated as advice, no ruling given)
claims.evidence: IslamQA (search snippets), https://islamqa.info/en/answers/81949/when-is-ghusl-required-and-when-is-it-mustahabb and https://islamqa.info/en/answers/975/causes-that-make-ghusl-a-must: 'The Malikis and Hanbalis are of the view that if a disbeliever becomes Muslim, ghusl is required ... The Hanafis and Shafi'is are of the view that it is encouraged'; 'If a disbeliever becomes Muslim when he is in the state of janabah, then he has to do ghusl.'

claims.claim: The Prophet told converts to make ghusl (basis of the practice)
claims.evidence: Sunnah.com (search snippet), https://sunnah.com/abudawud:355: Qays ibn Asim came to the Prophet intending to embrace Islam and was commanded to take a bath with water and lote-tree leaves; also in Tirmidhi and Nasa'i.

claims.claim: Ghusl on conversion is recommended, obligatory if in a state of major ritual impurity before praying
claims.evidence: SeekersGuidance (search snippet), https://seekersguidance.org/answers/islamic-belief/is-ghusl-required-after-saying-the-shahada-shaykh-abdul-rahim-reasat/: 'it is recommended that they perform a ritual bath'; 'only obligatory for the one who just enters Islam if they are in a state of major ritual impurity and are going to perform the prayers'.

rows.notes: Ghusl advice is consistent with the sources. The schools differ: Maliki and Hanbali say obligatory on conversion, Hanafi and Shafi'i say recommended unless the person was in a state of major impurity, in which case all agree it is needed before prayer. The description does not need to choose, but it could say 'before your first prayer'.
rows.method: 3 web searches (islamqa.info, sunnah.com, seekersguidance.org snippets); page fetch blocked

claims.claim: Hajj becomes an obligation once a person is able to go
claims.evidence: Quran.com, https://quran.com/ali-imran/97 (3:97): 'Pilgrimage to this House is an obligation by Allah upon whoever is able among the people'; the tafsir snippet on the same page explains 'able' as having sufficient provision and a means of transport, with a secure route.

claims.claim: Zakat becomes an obligation once its conditions (the nisab threshold) apply
claims.evidence: IslamQA, https://islamqa.info/en/answers/99381: if wealth falls short of the nisab, no zakah is due, and if it drops below the nisab during the year no zakah is due; https://islamqa.info/en/64: the nisab is 85 g of gold or 595 g of silver, the rate 2.5%, after one full lunar year.

rows.notes: Both statements are the standard Sunni position. Zakat also needs a full lunar year (hawl) on the wealth, which 'once the conditions apply' covers. Sending the reader to someone qualified is the right framing.

claims.evidence: from standard references (not confirmed online): Quran 2:187, eat and drink until the white thread of dawn is distinct from the black thread, then complete the fast until night; https://quran.com/2/187

claims.claim: 'In the Hanafi school' kissing or touching that leads to ejaculation breaks the fast
claims.evidence: from standard references (not confirmed online): all four Sunni schools hold that deliberate ejaculation from kissing or touching breaks the fast; they differ only on whether expiation is also due (Maliki: yes). The Hanafi label comes from the step's SeekersGuidance Hanafi source and implies the other schools allow it, which they do not.

claims.claim: The Prophet recommended breaking the fast with dates and water
claims.evidence: from standard references (not confirmed online): Sunan Abi Dawud 2356 (Anas): fresh dates, else dried dates, else sips of water; Sunan Abi Dawud 2355 and Tirmidhi 658 (Salman ibn Amir): break with dates, if not, water, for it is pure; https://sunnah.com/abudawud:2356. The step gives no hadith id for this.

claims.claim: Each day's fast needs a fresh intention (niyyah)
claims.evidence: from standard references (not confirmed online): this is the Hanafi, Shafi'i and Hanbali position; the Maliki school holds that one intention at the start of Ramadan covers the whole month if the fast is not interrupted. Stated as agreed.

rows.notes: Two scope problems: 'in the Hanafi school' marks a point all four schools agree on, so a non-Hanafi reader may think it does not break their fast; the daily-intention rule is stated as agreed although the Maliki school accepts one intention for the month. Add a hadith id for dates and water (Abu Dawud 2356). Suhoor line is fine (Bukhari 1923).
rows.method: Compared with standard fiqh references and the step's cited SeekersGuidance (Hanafi) source note; not confirmed online (search budget exhausted, fetch blocked).

claims.claim: Pregnant or breastfeeding women may be exempt if fasting puts them at risk
claims.evidence: from standard references (not confirmed online): Sunan Abi Dawud 2408 and Tirmidhi 715 (Anas ibn Malik al-Ka'bi): Allah relieved the traveller of fasting and half the prayer, and the pregnant and nursing woman of fasting. claims.claim: Women do not fast during menstruation and make the days up
claims.evidence: from standard references (not confirmed online): Sahih Muslim 335 and Bukhari 321 (Aisha, asked by Mu'adhah): we were ordered to make up the fasts but not the prayers; https://sunnah.com/muslim:335

claims.claim: Older people who cannot fast feed a person in need per day; children are not required to fast

rows.notes: All six points are the standard Sunni positions. Precision point only: for pregnant and nursing women the schools differ on whether make-up days, fidyah or both follow, which the step rightly leaves to a scholar. Not confirmed online this session.

claims.claim: Ramadan follows the lunar calendar, so the dates shift each year
claims.evidence: from standard references (not confirmed online): the Islamic year is 354 or 355 days, so Ramadan begins about 10 to 11 days earlier each Gregorian year.

claims.claim: The month starts with the sighting of the new moon

In Canada some communities follow a calculated calendar (Fiqh Council of North America) and others a regional sighting committee, so local start dates can differ.

claims.claim: Tarawih nightly prayers, community iftars and Eid al-Fitr at the end of the month
claims.evidence: from standard references (not confirmed online): standard practice; Sahih al-Bukhari 2009 on night prayer in Ramadan; Eid al-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal.

rows.notes: Accurate at the level written. Worth one line that Canadian masjids may announce different start dates because some use calculation and some local sighting. Not confirmed online this session.

claims.claim: Quran 113:5 seeks refuge from the envier; arrogance is looking down on people and refusing to accept truth

rows.notes: All quotations match. The anger advice has no reference on the page: sitting down (Abu Dawud 4782), silence (Ahmad, Adab al-Mufrad 1320) and seeking refuge (Bukhari 6115) are sound; the wudu report (Abu Dawud 4784) is graded weak by al-Albani and others, so cite the sound ones and present wudu as widely recommended rather than as a firm hadith. Arrogance definition is Muslim 91.

claims.claim: These habits are recommended, not obligations
claims.evidence: IslamQA and SeekersGuidance (search snippets): https://seekersguidance.org/answers/hanafi-fiqh/is-it-sinful-to-eat-with-the-left-hand/ treats the command as 'recommendation and propriety, and not of necessity', while https://islamqa.info/en/answers/3020 holds eating with the left hand prohibited and the right hand obligatory. The site states the majority view.

rows.notes: All three citations match Sunnah.com and Quran.com. 'Recommended, not obligations' is the position of the four schools for these habits, but a minority (Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Uthaymeen, IslamQA 3020) holds that eating with the right hand is obligatory; a phrase such as 'most scholars treat these as recommended' would cover it. Returning a greeting is obligatory; offering it is sunnah.

claims.claim: At Taif he prayed for their guidance instead of revenge; at the conquest of Makkah he forgave the city
claims.evidence: Sunnah.com (search snippet), https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3231: offered the Angel of the Mountains, he said 'No, but I hope that Allah will let them beget children who will worship Allah Alone'. IslamQA (search snippet), https://islamqa.info/en/answers/135590: at the conquest 'it was said to the people of Makkah: Go, for you are free' and he pardoned the Quraysh. The stoning until he bled comes from the sira (Ibn Hisham), not from Bukhari 3231.

claims.claim: He never turned away anyone who asked him for help
claims.evidence: Sunnah.com (search snippet), https://sunnah.com/muslim:2311a, Jabir: 'It never happened that Allah's Messenger was asked for anything and he said: No.'

rows.notes: Every seerah claim is supported by a sound report, but none is cited on the page; add Nasa'i 1141, Adab al-Mufrad 540-541, Bukhari 676, Bukhari 63, Bukhari 3231 and Muslim 2311 to sourceIds. Bukhari 3231 records hope for the Taif people's descendants rather than a prayer for the crowd itself. 'Generosity (sadaqah)' mislabels: sadaqah is voluntary charity, generosity is karam or jud.

claims.claim: Ontario: a dependant (spouse, former spouse, child, parent, sibling) can claim support from the estate, usually within 6 months of the estate trustee being named
claims.evidence: Succession Law Reform Act s.57 and s.61 via the e-Laws GitHub mirror (hordruma/elaws_scraper; official https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90s26): dependant means the spouse, a parent, a child or a brother or sister the deceased was supporting; 'no application ... may be made after six months from the grant of letters probate of the will or of letters of administration', with an exception for undistributed estate

claims.claim: Ontario: a married spouse chooses between the will and an equalization payment and must ask the court within 6 months of the death
claims.evidence: Family Law Act s.6(1), s.6(10) and s.7(3)(c) via the same mirror (official https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03): the surviving spouse 'shall elect to take under the will or to receive the entitlement under section 5'; the election is filed 'within six months after the first spouse's death'; an application shall not be brought after 'six months after the first spouse's death'

claims.evidence: SeekersGuidance (search snippet), https://seekersguidance.org/answers/hanafi-fiqh/is-kosher-meat-upon-which-gods-name-has-not-been-pronounced-permissible/: the Hanafi school makes pronouncing God's name a condition, so a Jewish slaughterer must pronounce it 'on each animal'; 'this is also the position of the Hanbali school'; in the Maliki and Shafi'i schools the slaughter of a Jew who did not pronounce it on every animal 'would be permitted' if the other conditions are met.

claims.claim: Cheese: the Hanafi school permits rennet from animals other than pigs; other schools are stricter
claims.evidence: SeekersGuidance (search snippet), https://seekersguidance.org/answers/hanafi-fiqh/is-rennet-in-cheese-halal-or-haram-to-consume/: 'Cheese made with animal rennet other than a pig source is halal' in the Hanafi school; 'it is better to avoid whenever reasonably possible when its source is unknown because of the difference of opinion between the Sunni schools'.

claims.claim: Hunting for food is permitted and for sport is not
claims.evidence: SeekersGuidance (search snippet), https://seekersguidance.org/answers/general-counsel/is-hunting-permissible/: 'Hunting for sport is not permissible'; the Prophet said 'Don't treat anything that has a soul as a target' (Sahih Muslim); killing an animal to benefit from its meat, skin or bones is permitted.

claims.claim: A Hanafi answer calls catch-and-release fishing impermissible
claims.evidence: SeekersGuidance (search snippet), https://seekersguidance.org/answers/fiqh-answers-2/what-is-the-ruling-of-catch-and-release-fishing-if-it-is-done-to-sharpen-skills-not-for-fun-or-sports/: 'impermissible ... even if it is done to sharpen skills', because it often leads to the death of the fish; alternative is to keep and eat a legal catch. The snippet did not name the school; the site's source record names Mawlana Ilyas Patel (Hanafi).

rows.notes: All four points match their SeekersGuidance answers and the FAQ (faq-lif-037, 038, 040). Precision points: 'require God's name' glosses over the forgetfulness exception in the Hanafi and Hanbali schools; the Maliki view is left out here though the FAQ gives it; the kosher answer itself concludes kosher meat can be eaten, which the guide leaves to the teacher.

claims.evidence: 211 Ontario (search snippets), https://211ontario.ca/contact/ and https://211ontario.ca/: 211 is 'a free and confidential service'; 'Text 2-1-1 is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Our helpline is answered by real people 24/7'; also toll-free 1-877-330-3213, 150+ languages; connects people to social services and community programs.

claims.claim: Asking for money and rushing you are warning signs
claims.evidence: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (search snippet), https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/scams-fraudes/romance-rencontre-eng.htm: fraudsters 'ask for money for travel, a medical emergency or family assistance - making it seem urgent'; warning signs include someone who 'professes their love' before meeting, 'discourages you from discussing them or their situation with your friends and family, attempting to isolate you', and who 'acts distressed or angry to guilt you into sending money'.

claims.claim: Telling you to keep things secret or cutting you off from family and other Muslims is a warning sign
claims.evidence: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (search snippet), https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/scams-fraudes/romance-rencontre-eng.htm: fraudsters 'ask for money for travel, a medical emergency or family assistance - making it seem urgent'; warning signs include someone who 'professes their love' before meeting, 'discourages you from discussing them or their situation with your friends and family, attempting to isolate you', and who 'acts distressed or angry to guilt you into sending money'. Public Safety Canada (search snippet), https://www.publicsafety.gc.ca/cnt/rsrcs/pblctns/ntnl-strtg-cntrng-rdc

rows.notes: Holds. Scope: 211 also operates outside Ontario (211.ca), so a Canada-wide FAQ could say so (not verified here). The CAFC wording is 'discourages you from discussing them with friends and family' rather than 'keep things secret'. The Public Safety strategy treats isolation as a risk factor and belonging as protective, not literally a 'recruitment tactic' as the source note puts it.
rows.method: 4 web searches (211ontario.ca, antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca x2, publicsafety.gc.ca snippets); page fetch blocked
